note.text:
Chemistry is everywhere in daily life:
• Health: medicines, vaccines, antiseptics.
• Farming: fertilisers make crops grow; pesticides protect them.
• Cleaning: soap and detergents; bleach.
• Clean water: chlorine kills germs in drinking water.
• Building: cement, paint, glass.
• Energy: fuels such as petrol, kerosene, cooking gas.
• Food: salt, sugar and vinegar keep food from going bad.
• Household goods: plastics, cloth, cosmetics.
Chemistry can also cause harm when it is misused: smoke and waste pollute air and rivers, and some chemicals are poisonous. Using chemicals carefully protects people and the environment.

worked_example.problem: Give two ways chemistry helps a farmer in the North West, and one way it can cause harm.
steps: Fertilisers help maize and beans grow better.
But too much fertiliser or pesticide can wash into streams and pollute the water.
worked_example.answer: Fertilisers and pesticides help; misused, they pollute streams.

cards.idea: Chemistry gives us medicines, fertilisers, soap, clean water, cement, fuels and plastics.
example: Chlorine in the water treatment plant kills germs, so tap water is safer to drink.

cards.idea: Chemistry helps keep food: salt, sugar and vinegar stop germs from growing.
example: Smoked and salted fish lasts longer than fresh fish.

cards.idea: Misused, chemicals can harm: smoke and waste pollute air and water, and some chemicals are poisonous.
example: Pouring used engine oil into a stream kills fish.

wrong.explain: Soap removes dirt and germs: a good use.

wrong.text: Using fertiliser on a maize farm.
